Its E2g line is real (about 15× noise, F-test strongly favours a peak) and is about 10% as strong as flake 1's (area ratio 0.105 ± 0.004). Monolayer hBN is consistent with this (E2g upshift and broadening, from literature I recalled but did not verify here), but few-layer flakes give similar signatures. The E2g intensity is not a calibrated thickness scale without a reference flake of known thickness on the same substrate and spot. The Si-normalised comparison that would usually help is unreliable here: the Si line differs by 19× between the two spectra, which a hBN layer on 290 nm SiO2/Si cannot produce in a simple interference model. Confirming monolayer needs AFM step height on flake 2, a same-spot Raman calibration against a flake of known thickness, and mapping across the flake.

observations.finding: Flake 1 shows a sharp E2g line of hBN at 1366.19 ± 0.04 cm⁻¹ with FWHM 17.9 cm⁻¹ and peak height ~3230 counts above a linear background (area 91011 ± 594). This is the expected bulk-like E2g position.
observations.evidence: Lorentzian + linear background fit over 1300–1440 cm⁻¹. Centre, FWHM and height are unchanged (within 0.1 cm⁻¹ / 1 %) across windows 1280–1460, 1320–1420 and 1300–1440, and with quadratic background. Residual SD ~40 counts.

observations.finding: Flake 2 has a weak but statistically real E2g-like peak at 1368.98 ± 0.24 cm⁻¹, FWHM 22.4 ± 0.9 cm⁻¹ (21–22.5 across fit choices), height ~271 counts, area 9551 ± 347. Its height is ~8% and its area ~10.5% of flake 1.
observations.evidence: Same fit model as flake 1. F-test versus a background-only model: F ≈ 290–1100 across windows and background orders. ΔBIC ≈ −260 to −630 in favour of the peak. Residual SD 18.5–19.3 counts, close to the point-to-point noise of ~18.5 counts estimated from 1500–1649 cm⁻¹. Area ratio flake2/flake1 = 0.105 ± 0.004 (statistical only).

observations.finding: The E2g position differs by +2.79 cm⁻¹ between flakes, and flake 2 is broader (22 vs 18 cm⁻¹). The wavenumber scale is consistent between runs, so this is not a calibration offset.
observations.evidence: Si 520 cm⁻¹ line fitted at 520.90 ± 0.06 cm⁻¹ (flake 1) and 520.90 ± 0.00 cm⁻¹ (flake 2), FWHM 3.31 and 3.50 cm⁻¹ (instrument resolution ~3.3–3.5 cm⁻¹). Si literature value ~520.7 cm⁻¹ implies a small +0.2 cm⁻¹ offset, applied to both.

observations.finding: The Si 520 line is 19.4× stronger in flake 2 than in flake 1 (area 98965 vs 5093; height 18013 vs 979). The E2g/Si ratio therefore differs by ~185× between flakes. observations.evidence: Transfer-matrix estimate, normal incidence, 514.5 nm, 290 nm SiO2 (n=1.46), Si (n=4.29+0.07i), hBN n=1.6/1.95/2.2 (assumed). Si signal (|E|⁴ at Si surface, relative to bare SiO2/Si) varies over 0–400 nm of hBN by at most ~2.6×, ~4.4× and ~6.2× for the three indices. Over 0–30 nm the drop is 0.27–0.59 (i.e. up to ~4×).

observations.finding: Flake 2 has a flat, elevated background (~1450 counts at 450 cm⁻¹, ~1700 at 1000 cm⁻¹, ~1550 near the E2g band) compared with flake 1 (~440 at 450 cm⁻¹, ~1100 near 1500 cm⁻¹). This is not an hBN Raman feature.
observations.evidence: Baseline from 5th-percentile running filter (200 cm⁻¹ window) and direct sampling of the spectra. Flake 2 median 1670 counts vs flake 1 median 1003 counts over the full range.

observations.finding: A 0.105 area ratio is consistent with flake 2 being roughly one-tenth of flake 1's E2g intensity, which would make flake 2 a monolayer only if flake 1 were ~10 layers. observations.evidence: Lorentzian + linear background fit over 1300–1440 cm⁻¹. Centre, FWHM and height are unchanged (within 0.1 cm⁻¹ / 1 %) across windows 1280–1460, 1320–1420 and 1300–1440, and with quadratic background. Residual SD ~40 counts.

observations.finding: Flake 2 has a weak but statistically real E2g-like peak at 1368.98 ± 0.24 cm⁻¹, FWHM 22.4 ± 0.9 cm⁻¹ (21–22.5 across fit choices), height ~271 counts, area 9551 ± 347. Its height is ~8% and its area ~10.5% of flake 1.
observations.evidence: Same fit model as flake 1. F-test versus a background-only model: F ≈ 290–1100 across windows and background orders. ΔBIC ≈ −260 to −630 in favour of the peak. Residual SD 18.5–19.3 counts, close to the point-to-point noise of ~18.5 counts estimated from 1500–1649 cm⁻¹. Area ratio flake2/flake1 = 0.105 ± 0.004 (statistical only).

observations.finding: The E2g position differs by +2.79 cm⁻¹ between flakes, and flake 2 is broader (22 vs 18 cm⁻¹). The wavenumber scale is consistent between runs, so this is not a calibration offset.
observations.evidence: Si 520 cm⁻¹ line fitted at 520.90 ± 0.06 cm⁻¹ (flake 1) and 520.90 ± 0.00 cm⁻¹ (flake 2), FWHM 3.31 and 3.50 cm⁻¹ (instrument resolution ~3.3–3.5 cm⁻¹). Si literature value ~520.7 cm⁻¹ implies a small +0.2 cm⁻¹ offset, applied to both.

observations.finding: The Si 520 line is 19.4× stronger in flake 2 than in flake 1 (area 98965 vs 5093; height 18013 vs 979). The E2g/Si ratio therefore differs by ~185× between flakes. A hBN layer on 290 nm SiO2/Si cannot account for this, so the Si line is not a usable thickness reference across these two spectra.
observations.evidence: Transfer-matrix estimate, normal incidence, 514.5 nm, 290 nm SiO2 (n=1.46), Si (n=4.29+0.07i), hBN n=1.6/1.95/2.2 (assumed). Si signal (|E|⁴ at Si surface, relative to bare SiO2/Si) varies over 0–400 nm of hBN by at most ~2.6×, ~4.4× and ~6.2× for the three indices. Over 0–30 nm the drop is 0.27–0.59 (i.e. up to ~4×).

observations.finding: Flake 2 has a flat, elevated background (~1450 counts at 450 cm⁻¹, ~1700 at 1000 cm⁻¹, ~1550 near the E2g band) compared with flake 1 (~440 at 450 cm⁻¹, ~1100 near 1500 cm⁻¹). This is not an hBN Raman feature.
observations.evidence: Baseline from 5th-percentile running filter (200 cm⁻¹ window) and direct sampling of the spectra. Flake 2 median 1670 counts vs flake 1 median 1003 counts over the full range.

observations.finding: A 0.105 area ratio is consistent with flake 2 being roughly one-tenth of flake 1's E2g intensity, which would make flake 2 a monolayer only if flake 1 were ~10 layers. Flake 1's thickness is not known, and interference modulates the E2g intensity, so the ratio gives only a rough layer-count scaling.
observations.evidence: If E2g intensity were linear in layer number, N2 ≈ 0.105 × N1. Interference effects estimated above change the Si signal by ~2–4× for thin hBN, so the E2g scaling is probably uncertain by a similar factor.

observations.finding: Monolayer hBN is reported to show an E2g upshift and a linewidth change relative to bulk (roughly 1369 vs 1366 cm⁻¹), which would match flake 2's position. I recalled this from memory and did not verify the numbers against the paper's figure here, so treat it as unconfirmed.

caveats: The 19× Si difference is the main artifact risk. The two spectra have different x-steps (0.783 vs 0.750 cm⁻¹), so the acquisition settings or grating probably differed. Focus, spot position, collection efficiency or the Si/SiO2 region could also differ. These spectra should not be used for intensity-based thickness comparisons without a same-session calibration.

Flake 2's baseline is elevated (~500 counts over flake 1). This could be residue fluorescence (PMMA or adhesive) or substrate background, and it is not hBN. A nearby bare SiO2 spectrum would test this.

The flake 2 E2g peak is weak (height ~270 counts, SNR ~15). Its position and width depend on the background model. The 2.8 cm⁻¹ shift is well above the fit error (0.25 cm⁻¹) and calibration offset (0.2 cm⁻¹), but the fit is still sensitive to baseline shape at the ~0.1–0.2 cm⁻¹ level.

The hBN refractive indices used (1.6, 1.95, 2.2) are assumptions because hBN is anisotropic in the visible. The transfer-matrix estimate is a simplified normal-incidence model using |E|⁴ at the Si surface, ignoring the depth profile and collection geometry. It is used only to bound the Si attenuation, not to predict absolute intensities.

Literature values (E2g position and width in bulk and monolayer hBN) are from memory and have not been checked against the papers in this session. The Gorbachev 2011 numbers in particular need verification before being quoted.

Monolayer and few-layer hBN Raman spectra are similar apart from weak changes in position and width, so an E2g line alone cannot identify a monolayer. Optical contrast on 290 nm SiO2 is also weak for hBN, so 'barely visible' says flake 2 is thin but does not give a layer count.
questions_for_user: What is the thickness of flake 1 (AFM or profilometry)? Together with the E2g area ratio of 0.105, this would give a rough layer count for flake 2. The ratio alone cannot.

Were both spectra taken in one session with the same grating, spot size, focus and objective? The x-steps differ (0.783 vs 0.750 cm⁻¹), and the Si line differs by 19×, so I need to know whether intensities are comparable at all.
What is the AFM height (step) of flake 2, and is it a single step on the substrate? This is the most direct test of monolayer.

Why is the flake 2 background about 500 counts higher? Was there residue from the transfer (PMMA, adhesive) or a thicker substrate region? A bare-SiO2 spectrum measured under the same conditions would settle this.

Was the laser power at the sample measured? The E2g position is sensitive to heating. A thin, poorly conducting flake would heat more and redshift, which is the opposite of the observed upshift, so heating is unlikely to explain it, but I want to confirm the power was low and equal for both flakes.

Can you map E2g across flake 2 (and check the edges)? A uniform E2g intensity and position across the flake, with no step at the edges, would support a single-layer or uniform few-layer flake. A single spot cannot show that.
